insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (examples shown: ₹1.5L, ₹2L, ₹3L, ₹4L, ₹5L, ₹10L, ₹15L; Gold Plan shows up to ₹25L)

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months (Pre-existing diseases)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer
good.reference: Section IV. EXCLUSIONS > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage (industry-standard; not a red flag as per rules).

good.name: Specific disease/procedure waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Section IV. EXCLUSIONS > 2. Speciﬁed disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Listed specified illnesses/procedures are covered after 24 months (standard).

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (except accident)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section IV. EXCLUSIONS > 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Non-accident illnesses have a 30-day initial waiting period (standard).

good.name: Restore benefit: 200% restore once per policy year, but only for unrelated illnesses (not for Modern Treatment)
good.quote: There shall be automatic restoration of the Basic Sum Insured by 200%, once during the policy period... such restored Basic Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness / disease unrelated to the illness / diseases for which claim/s was / were made... This beneﬁt is not available for Modern Treatment
good.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > K. Automatic Restoration of Basic Sum Insured (Page 3/9)
good.explanation: Your Sum Insured can be restored after it is exhausted, but it can be used only for unrelated conditions—so it is a standard restore (not same-illness).

good.name: Co-pay: 10% for entry age 61+ (waived if you entered before 61 and renewed continuously)
good.quote: This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry in to this policy is 61 years and above. This co-payment will not apply for those insured persons who have entered the policy before attaining 61 years of age and renew the policy continuously without any break
good.reference: Important Note : Applicable for II Coverage and Optional Covers > Point 6 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: If you join at age 61+, you pay 10% of each claim (standard senior co-pay). If you joined earlier than 61 and keep renewing without break, the co-pay does not apply.

bad.name: Room rent: daily cap (leads to proportionate deductions on associated medical expenses)
bad.quote: Basic Sum Insured Rs Limits (Rs) 1,50,000/- 2% of Basic Sum Insured maximum of Rs.5,000/- per day
bad.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > A. Room, boarding, nursing expenses... (Page 2/9)
bad.explanation: A daily room rent cap is a red flag because it can force you into a lower room category or trigger proportionate deductions.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction applicable due to room rent eligibility limits (associated medical expenses)
bad.quote: Expenses relating to Associated Medical Expenses will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > Note under A (Page 2/9)
bad.explanation: Because room rent is capped/room-category-linked, the insurer can reduce payouts for associated medical expenses proportionately if you choose a higher room than eligible.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (out-of-pocket list included as items to be subsumed/packaged)
bad.quote: ITEMS THAT ARE TO BE SUBSUMED INTO PROCEDURE CHARGES... DISPOSABLES RAZORS CHARGES... SURGICAL BLADES... GAUZE... SURGICAL TAPE...
bad.reference: Annexure/List: ITEMS THAT ARE TO BE SUBSUMED... (Page 9/9)
bad.explanation: The wording lists many consumable-type items as bundled/subsumed rather than explicitly covered as a benefit. Since explicit “consumables covered” is not stated, treat as not covered for the mandatory reporting—expect out-of-pocket consumables depending on hospital billing.

bad.name: Pre-hospitalization: only 30 days
bad.quote: Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of hospitalization
bad.explanation: 30 days is the minimum standard; anything below 30 is worse, but 30 days still counts as weak vs better policies offering 60+ days.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization: 60 days with additional payout cap (7% and max ₹5,000 per hospitalization)
bad.quote: Post Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period up to 60 days... The amount payable shall not exceed the sum equivalent to 7% of the hospitalization expenses subject to a maximum of Rs.5,000/- per hospitalisation.
bad.explanation: While 60 days is the minimum acceptable duration, the additional 7%/₹5,000 cap can significantly limit reimbursements for follow-up medicines/tests.

bad.name: NCB/Cumulative Bonus reduces on claims (can drop to zero)
bad.quote: In the event of a claim resulting in... At any point of time, the cumulative bonus will not be less than “zero”... the cumulative bonus granted on renewal will be “nil” or “zero”
bad.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > J. Cumulative Bonus (Special Conditions) (Page 3/9)
bad.explanation: This bonus is not protected; it reduces with claims and can become nil/zero, which is a negative vs non-resetting renewal bonuses.

unclear.name: Cashless network size (number of network hospitals) not stated
unclear.quote: Cashless facility can be availed only in networked Hospitals. For details of Networked Hospitals, the insured may visit www.starhealth.in or contact the nearest branch
unclear.reference: Section V. CONDITIONS > 2.B Documents for Cashless Treatment (Page 6/9)
unclear.explanation: The document confirms cashless is only at network hospitals, but does not specify the network size (e.g., 7,000/10,000+). Verify current network count for your city.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
